rationale:
Evidence: across 120 development trials (iterations 0 to 2), no run finished. Every run ended off track at progress 0.10 to 0.15, and max_error sat at about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is 0.06 m for any allowed body width). The s-bend progress was 0.1475 in every iteration, so the failure point is nearly fixed by the track and not by any one setting. Steering oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.15), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts off the tape in one large excursion, with RMS error of about 0.025 to 0.03 m, which is about twice the half-width.

What the comparisons show: iteration 0 (kp 3.0, kd 0.5, base 1.6, 12 mm sensors) scored best at 53.0. Iteration 2 raised kp to 4.5 and kd to 1.0, and its score fell to 50.5. Iteration 1 also used kp 4.5 and was the lowest at 50.6, although it changed several things at once. The most consistent signal is that the higher kp did not help, which suggests the robot overcorrects or reacts too late at speed.

Changes: (1) Return kp to 2.5, between the best-scoring 3.0 and the lower value, to reduce overshoot. (2) Keep kd at 0.8 to damp the response without the heavier derivative of iteration 2. (3) Keep ki at 0.05, the iteration 0 value, since the integral has not been shown to matter. (4) Move the sensor row forward only to y = 0.03 m, from 0.04 m, to shorten the lag between the sensed line and the axle, which is the pivot. (5) Keep the 12 mm sensors and the iteration 0 geometry otherwise, and lower base_speed to 1.4 so there is more time to correct on the bends. This keeps the change set small and lets the next race attribute any gain to the gain and lag changes.

Expected result: fewer large excursions, so max_error should stay nearer 0.05 m and progress should rise somewhat above 0.15 on the s-bend. A score in the 53 to 56 range is plausible. Completion is still unlikely, because the average speed needed for the 3 s limit is near 1.5 m/s, and base_speed 1.4 lowers it. If progress improves without a finish, the following iteration should raise base_speed again.
